items.followUp: Define force and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines momentum in terms of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition or formula.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.description: Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹ (or N s).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct unit.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹ (or N s).

items.followUp: State one difference between heat energy and electrical energy.

rubric.why: Describes sound energy as requiring a material medium.
rubric.description: Sound energy is mechanical and cannot travel through a vacuum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sound needs a medium or cannot travel in a vacuum.

rubric.why: Distinguishes light energy by its ability to travel through a vacuum.
rubric.description: Light energy is electromagnetic and can travel through a vacuum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light can travel in a vacuum or does not need a medium.

modelAnswer: Sound energy is mechanical and requires a material medium to travel.
Light energy is electromagnetic and can travel through a vacuum.

items.followUp: What is meant by ionisation of a gas?

rubric.why: Names the fourth state of matter.
rubric.description: The fourth state of matter is called plasma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plasma as the fourth state.

rubric.description: Plasma is an ionised gas containing positive ions and free electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing plasma as an ionised gas or identifying its charged particles.

modelAnswer: Yes. The fourth state of matter is called plasma.
It is an ionised gas containing positive ions and free electrons.

items.followUp: What is meant by a laboratory thermometer?

rubric.why: States the purpose of a clinical thermometer.
rubric.description: A clinical thermometer is used to measure human body temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its use in measuring body temperature.

rubric.why: Gives the usual temperature range of a clinical thermometer.
rubric.description: Its usual range is 35°C to 42°C (or 94°F to 108°F).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct range in either scale.

modelAnswer: A clinical thermometer is used to measure human body temperature.
Its usual range is 35°C to 42°C (94°F to 108°F).

items.followUp: Convert 104°F into Celsius and Kelvin scales.

rubric.why: Identifies the temperature given in the question.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly recording the given temperature.

rubric.why: Uses the correct Fahrenheit-to-Celsius conversion relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Shows the conversion and obtains the correct Celsius temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for 37°C.

rubric.why: Converts the Celsius result to Kelvin correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct Kelvin conversion and result.

items.followUp: What is a derived quantity? Give two examples.

rubric.why: Defines a physical quantity as measurable and expressible with a value and unit.
rubric.description: A physical quantity is a property that can be measured and expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition including measurability and magnitude/unit.
Award 1 mark for any two valid physical quantities.

modelAnswer: A physical quantity is a property that can be measured and expressed by a magnitude and a unit.

items.followUp: How many significant figures are in 0.00450 m? Explain briefly.

rubric.why: Describes which digits are counted as significant figures.
rubric.description: Significant figures include all accurately known digits and the first doubtful digit.

rubric.why: Gives a suitable example and identifies its significant figures.
rubric.description: For example, 2.34 cm has three significant figures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example with the correct number of significant figures.

modelAnswer: Significant figures are all the accurately known digits in a measurement together with the first doubtful digit.
For example, 2.34 cm has three significant figures.

items.followUp: What is the prefix milli- equal to? Give an example of its use.

rubric.why: Explains the function of prefixes in measurement.
rubric.description: Prefixes are placed before units to represent multiples or submultiples of the units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that prefixes modify units to show multiples or submultiples.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of a prefix.
rubric.description: For example, kilo- means 10³, so 1 km = 1000 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct prefix and example.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are placed before units to represent multiples or submultiples of those units.
For example, kilo- means 10³, so 1 km = 1000 m.
